name: v3.28.0 - Archive and restore finished plans
body:
## Added

- Opt-in archive and restore for named plans. `set-active-plan.sh --archive <id>` (PowerShell: `-Archive <id>`) previews the move to `.planning/.archive/<id>/`, `--yes` (`-Yes`) applies it, and `--restore <id>` moves a plan back the same way. The directory moves with its sidecars in a single rename. Nothing is deleted and nothing is archived automatically. The shared `.active_plan` pointer is cleared only when it names the archived plan, and an ID must match the directory name exactly, including case. `--list --archived` lists archived plans, and the JSON inventory reports `archived_count` (#355).
- When a project holds several named plans and no `PLAN_ID` is set, hooks inject nothing. The multiple-plans notice now names the archive command. Once one named plan remains, hooks select it again without `PLAN_ID`.

## Fixed

- PowerShell inventory `modified_at` values no longer shift by the local UTC offset.
- The shell inventory reports a plan file held open by another process as unreadable instead of emitting invalid JSON.
- PowerShell 7 lists and resolves plans whose paths reach 260 characters.
- `set-active-plan.ps1 -List -Json` works inside a PowerShell session and through `-Command`, `-f` or a positional script path. A direct `-File` run writes one UTF-8 line; the other call forms return the same JSON with non-ASCII characters escaped, within the same 16 KiB limit.
- The shell inventory keeps non-ASCII project paths correct under `LC_ALL=C`.
- PowerShell listing and plan resolution include directories with the Windows Hidden attribute, matching the shell route.

The npm package and the ClawHub listing are updated separately.

name: v3.27.0 - Agent-readable plan inventory
body:
Planning agents can request a bounded JSON inventory from the existing listing helpers with `--list --json` or PowerShell `-List -Json`. It includes root and named planning-file paths, availability, phase metadata, shared defaults and explicit selection uncertainty. Inventory remains read-only and runs only when requested.

Claude plugin commands now follow the selected-plan and initializer contracts. The updates preserve valid pinned legacy roots, initialize from the validated project root, keep status reads compact and delegate attestation to the shipped helpers.

The schema/reference is included across supported installs. Human listing, ordinary activation, hooks and model settings keep their existing behavior. This release adds no dependency or automatic cleanup.

The README now opens with contributor portraits and a centered, collapsed community showcase. Five additions link to primary sources for extensions, ports, SDK adaptations and older bundled snapshots.

The canonical [planning-with-files@3.27.0 npm package](https://www.npmjs.com/package/planning-with-files/v/3.27.0) is published. Its registry archive matches the audited Git-source package byte for byte.

name: v3.25.2 - trackable plan creation and harness fixes
body:
Plan creation now requires the bundled initializer and explicit native format validation. `check-complete.sh --validate` and PowerShell `-Validate` reject plans with no recognized phases or missing/ambiguous native phase statuses. `plan-doctor.sh` reports these problems. Validation reads the plan without rewriting it or changing attestation; ordinary advisory and gated stop behavior is preserved.

The two saved blind cases that previously produced zero recognized phases were rerun with the updated skill. Both invoked the initializer, passed functional checks, and finished with five recognized, completed phases. Only these two behavioral cases were rerun.

Copilot startup and post-tool context now uses the current harness's top-level `additionalContext` output. The guide explains the legacy VS Code Local migration boundary. Cursor bash hooks consistently select named plans and refuse ambiguous or invalid selection without falling back to an unrelated root plan. Cursor installation documentation preserves existing registrations and avoids nested adapter directories (PRs #340, #341, #342).

The optional skill-lens evaluation now uses 0.25.0 and includes a two-session resume case. A maintainer follow-up prevents phase assertions from skipping to a subsection's status. Reported model measurements remain attributed to the contributor's original runs (PR #338).

name: v3.25.1 - status validity and optional eval
body:
OpenCode status now distinguishes an existing attestation marker from a valid digest for the current plan. `attested` keeps its presence-only meaning; `attestationValid` requires a digest check. Root and named legacy plans with oversized, unreadable or disappearing markers report false validity (PR #331, #330).

DSH `/pwf-status` now preserves the `PLAN_ID` selection notice when several plans exist. A project with no plan still gets the initialization message (PR #333, #332).

An optional skill-lens evaluation compares planning-file creation with and without the skill. Its guide records contributor-reported measurements, the checks' limits and paid-run requirements. Framework script execution requires a sandbox backend; the evaluation is outside normal CI (PR #334).

The OpenCode plugin source is version 1.2.1 and the DSH plugin source is version 1.0.2. npm distribution and the ClawHub website upload are separate publication steps.

name: v3.25.0 - Hermes plans per conversation
body:
Hermes adapter 0.3.0 lets conversations sharing a backend select different named plans.

- `planning_with_files_select` selects or clears a conversation's plan, including a plan in another project. Successful named initialization also selects its new plan.
- Reading a named `task_plan.md` selects it only for an unbound conversation. Successful writes and patches can switch to one unambiguous plan; failures, reference reads and patches spanning several plans preserve the existing selection.
- Profile-local records survive backend restarts. Hooks, tools, commands, reminders and the completion gate apply request-local selectors without changing the process environment.
- Missing or invalid selected plans fail closed, and conflicting explicit directory arguments return an error. Existing ambiguity refusal, attachment admission, link checks and attestation remain active.

Usage and host-version limits: [Select a plan per conversation](https://github.com/OthmanAdi/planning-with-files/blob/v3.25.0/docs/hermes.md#select-a-plan-per-conversation).

Validation includes 109 passing Hermes tests, 22 independent edge checks and 25 checks through the installed Hermes plugin/tool dispatch, including two threads making 60 hook calls each. The host smoke runs offline; live gateway and Desktop transport acceptance was not performed.

[Full CI](https://github.com/OthmanAdi/planning-with-files/actions/runs/39427343243) passed on the release commit: Ubuntu 1,090 tests, macOS 1,187, Windows 1,219, plus Pi 95, OpenCode 51 and DSH 49.

name: v3.24.3 - Pi snapshot attestation
body:
Pi extension 1.2.8 now verifies the same raw plan snapshot used for injected text and phase counts. Replacing the live file between reading and checking can no longer make a different snapshot pass attestation. Missing or unreadable selected approvals remain blocking failures.

The attestation guide clarifies that checkbox, phase-status and Next Step edits require explicit re-attestation. Strict behavior remains unchanged. The optional checkbox-policy discussion in #326 stays open; this release adds no automatic re-attestation or progress subsystem.

name: v3.24.2 - Suppress unchanged Pi plan reminders
body:
Pi parity mode now suppresses unchanged pre-tool plan views after confirmed turn-start context insertion. A visible plan edit queues one refresh, while selection changes, recovery events and failed or aborted runs invalidate delivery state. Turn-start context, execution approval and whole-plan attestation remain in place. `PWF_PRETOOL=always` restores the previous per-leaf Pi reminders.

The bundled Pi extension is 1.2.7. This change adds no dependencies or persistent cache files. Message scheduling tests do not establish provider billing savings.

Contributor totals now include reporters and testers, and the README portraits cover all 104 credited community contributors.

name: v3.24.0: Qoder CLI and less repeated plan context
body:
Native Qoder CLI support and less repeated planning context in Claude Code.

- The Qoder plugin installs the planning skill and seven lifecycle hooks. Its launcher uses isolated Python startup through Bash, and the adapter maps the optional completion gate to Qoder CLI's Stop exit-code contract. Claude-specific command prompts are excluded. Qoder CLI 1.1.67 validation, isolated installation and direct execution of installed hook descriptors passed; Qoder IDE behavior remains unverified (#313).
- Claude Code plugin and standalone skill hooks suppress unchanged PreToolUse views after successful prompt injection. A changed visible view refreshes once. Sessions, agents, selected plans and rendering modes have separate state; recovery resets it even when the plan is temporarily absent. Missing identity or an unsafe or unavailable cache preserves repeated injection. `PWF_PRETOOL=always` requests context on every matched tool call. Selection, snapshot and attestation checks still run before suppression (#312).
- File-only SessionStart recovery starts its catch-up child with isolated Python startup, preventing `PYTHONPATH` startup code from loading in that child.

The full test workflow passed before integration and on release commit 7056ed2f2b86a8a9e18840f625ac66a48fa07693: Python on Linux, Windows and macOS, plus the Pi, OpenCode and DSH suites. Contributor commits retain their original authors.

body:

Sessions moved to another project or subdirectory now use their current planning files. Installation instructions cover the v2 `plugins` key and the default export required by local wrappers.

name: v3.21.0 - Explicit attestation targets and pointer race recovery
body:
`attest-plan.sh` can now attest a root roadmap while a named ticket plan remains active. Use `--target root` or `--target <plan-id>`; the selection honors `PWF_PLAN_ROOT`, refuses invalid or linked targets, and prints the resolved paths before writing. Empty targets and unsupported trailing arguments fail without touching another plan.

PowerShell named-plan initialization now retries the transient active-pointer pre-check failure during concurrent replacement. Each attempt retains root and pointer validation, with a fixed retry bound.

Closes #294 and #296 through PRs #295 and #297.

### Thanks
@tayfuryldz, for both contributions and their regression coverage. The contribution entries are in CONTRIBUTORS.md.

name: v3.20.8 - Quiet Stop hook, current Cursor and Gemini hook schemas, owned pointer backups
body:
## What changed

- **Claude Code no longer shows a notice after every reply in sessions without a plan.** The Stop hook runs `check-complete --gate`, whose no-plan branch printed "No task_plan.md found" on every turn. The automatic check is now silent when there is no plan; the explicit report (`check-complete` without `--gate`) still prints the notice (#288, PR #289).
- **PowerShell pointer replacement cleans up only what it owns.** `set-active-plan.ps1` names its own backup file for `ReplaceFile`. If the final replacement fails after the old pointer was moved aside, it moves the pointer back, or deletes only its own backup when another selector has already written a safe pointer. It no longer leaves an unowned `.active_plan~RF*.TMP` and never deletes one it did not create. After a successful switch a backup that cannot be removed right away produces a warning, not a failed exit (#254, PR #290).
- **Cursor hooks match Cursor's current hook schema.** Cursor has no `userPromptSubmit` event, so the plan was never injected. Plan context now arrives through `sessionStart` `additional_context`, `preToolUse` answers `{"permission":"allow"}`, the progress reminder is `postToolUse` `additional_context`, failure paths print valid JSON, and the Windows hooks start PowerShell with `-NoProfile`. The shell session-start hook runs Python in isolated mode. Cursor Cloud Agents do not run `sessionStart` (#262, PR #291).
- **The Cursor stop hook is silent once every phase is complete.** Cursor submits a stop hook's `followup_message` as the next user message, and the hook sent "ALL PHASES COMPLETE" for a finished plan, so every stop triggered up to three automatic follow-up turns on the Windows route. An incomplete plan still asks Cursor to continue.
- **Gemini CLI hooks use the fields Gemini reads.** Plan context moves to `BeforeAgent` `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext`, and the `AfterTool` reminder moves into `hookSpecificOutput`. The old `BeforeTool` output was only shown to the user and the `BeforeModel` output was ignored (#292, PR #293).
- **The Cursor and Gemini hook scripts are executable.** Gemini runs each hook as `bash -c <path>` and Cursor requires executable script hooks. The Gemini hooks and the Cursor `pre-tool-use`, `post-tool-use` and `stop` hooks had been committed as 100644, so they could not run from a macOS or Linux clone. On macOS and Linux this also turns on the documented Cursor stop hook, which asks Cursor to continue an incomplete root plan at most three times per stop (`loop_limit`), as the Windows route already did. A test now checks the mode of every script the two manifests run by path.

## Upgrade note

If you copied the Cursor or Gemini adapter into a project, copy the manifest together with the scripts: `.cursor/hooks.json` and `.cursor/hooks.windows.json` now register `sessionStart`, and `.gemini/settings.json` registers `BeforeAgent` with `before-agent.sh`, which replaces `before-tool.sh` and `before-model.sh`.

## Thanks

- @mmychu for tracing the per-reply Stop notice and fixing every copy (PR #289)
- @kuei51307-hub for the caller-owned `ReplaceFile` backup with pointer recovery (PR #290)
- @SomSamantray for moving the Cursor hooks to the current schema (PR #291)
- @ShaunLinTW for reporting and fixing the Gemini hook output schema (#292, PR #293)

name: v3.20.6 - Pointer safety and official npm skill
body:
### Added

- The README ends with a linked portrait grid of credited contributors, excluding the maintainer.

- Hermes rejects linked active-plan pointers and replaces the pointer without modifying a hard-linked sibling (#259, PR #284).
- PowerShell named-plan initialization rejects a read-only active pointer before creating the new plan directory (#253, PR #285).
- PowerShell initialization works from a project path containing `[` or `]` under Windows PowerShell 5.1 (#256, PR #286).
- PowerShell active-pointer replacement retries transient concurrent I/O and pointer-inspection races while rechecking root and pointer safety (#254, PR #287). Cleanup after final `ReplaceFile` failure remains open in #254.

name: v3.20.5 - Reliable initialization and OpenCode replay
body:
### Fixed
- OpenCode session replay tolerates null or array part rows, non-string tool names, and non-string text instead of aborting the session. Healthy rows remain available, and the defensive checks are synchronized across the copies that carry this formatter (#269, PR #273).
- Shell and PowerShell initialization now report failed attestation as `NOT attested`, with a reason and recovery command, instead of claiming success. Attestation failure remains non-aborting, and inherited plan selectors are restored after the attempt (#276, PR #277).
- The analytics task-plan template includes a non-empty `## Next Step` section across its shipped copies. Structural and initializer regressions keep generated analytics plans compatible with lifecycles that require that section (#278, PR #279).
- PowerShell planning-file writes fail with a non-zero exit status and an error when access is denied. Named plans become active only after all three planning files are ready, so a failed initialization preserves the previous active pointer. The separately maintained host and translated initializers also stop on write errors (#255, PR #280).


planning-with-files@3.20.5 is published on npm. The ClawHub upload folder is prepared and verified; the website upload remains manual.

name: v3.20.4 - PowerShell route works in projects under OneDrive
body:
Two maintainer-found bugs, fixes #275 and #274.

**PowerShell route on OneDrive (#275).** `resolve-plan-dir.ps1`, the Cursor hook `resolve-plan-context.ps1` and `set-active-plan.ps1` refused an `.active_plan` pointer that carried the `ReparsePoint` file attribute. OneDrive Files On-Demand sets that attribute on every synced file, so in a project under OneDrive (the default `Documents` under Known Folder Move) the Cursor hooks stopped with the unsafe-pointer notice instead of injecting the pointed plan, the resolver printed nothing for `attest-plan.ps1` and `check-complete.ps1`, and `set-active-plan.ps1` refused to write. Every other route read the pointer normally. The three checks now refuse a container or a `LinkType` of `SymbolicLink` or `Junction`, the predicate v3.20.3 gave the directory checks and the `[ -L ]` of the shell scripts. A symlinked pointer is still refused; a hard-linked or placeholder pointer is a plain file, as it is to `sh`. The review of this fix found the same class of check in `attest-plan.ps1`'s native helper: it refused to hash, show or clear any reparse-point file, so attestation failed in every project under OneDrive while `init-session.ps1` still reported the plan as attested. It now refuses only name-surrogate reparse points (symlinks, junctions and unknown surrogate tags), the set Windows path parsing follows, so the security property is unchanged.

**Test guard walked the whole checkout (#274).** `tests/test_session_catchup_copies_exact_basename.py` loaded any `session-catchup.py` it found under the repository root, tracked or not. A stale clone kept under the gitignored `.planning/` on a maintainer machine failed the two tests with 120 subtests while CI stayed green. The copies now come from `git ls-files`; the filtered walk is kept only for a checkout without git.

No shipped script other than the three PowerShell files changed; every mirror is synced.

name: v3.20.3 - linked plan directories are never plans, on every route
body:
Fixes #270: a symlinked or junctioned directory under `.planning/` is never a plan, on every route that resolves plans.

**What was wrong.** `inject-plan.sh` and `resolve-plan-dir.sh --check-ambiguity` counted a linked plan directory toward the several-plans rule while the Hermes plugin did not, so with one real plan and one linked plan the shell route refused with the `Multiple plans are available` notice and Hermes injected the real plan.

**What the fix does.**
- The shell counters skip linked directories (PR #271 by @ShaunLinTW). Skipping the link in the counter alone left the selection paths following it through containment: the tree then counted as one plan and the newest-mtime scan could select the linked directory, the mtime guess the #240 rule exists to prevent. The shell family (`resolve-plan-dir.sh`, `inject-plan.sh`, `resolve-plan-dir.ps1`, the Python twin `inject-plan.py`) therefore refuses a linked plan directory in the `PLAN_ID`, `.active_plan` and newest-mtime branches as well. A `PLAN_ID` naming one fails closed with the existing "does not name a plan directory" notice; a pointer naming one falls through like a stale pointer.
- The Codex adapter and the OpenCode and DeepSeek Harness plugin cores skip linked directories in their counters, which their selection already did.
- `set-active-plan.sh` and `set-active-plan.ps1` refuse to point the shared default at a linked directory and leave it out of `--list`.
- The link test is symlink or junction only (`[ -L ]`, `is_link`, `LinkType`), never the bare ReparsePoint attribute: OneDrive Files On-Demand marks every synced directory as a reparse point, and those stay plans. The first build of this release tested the attribute in PowerShell and would have silenced the Cursor route on OneDrive projects; the review caught it before the tag.
- Untouched on purpose: the Pi extension keeps its armed-only containment rule, and the nested-root probes still count a linked nested plan as a conflict, which only ever refuses.

Every shipped copy is synced. The sh/py parity suite, the cross-route ambiguity suite, the pointer tool suite, the Codex suite and both plugin vitest suites carry the linked-directory fixture (junction on Windows, symlink elsewhere).

### Thanks
- @ShaunLinTW, for the shell counter change with the Hermes differential regression in #271.

name: v3.20.2 - Hermes: say why nothing was injected when the host re-homes the working directory
body:
Hermes plugin 0.2.2, fixes #272.

**What was wrong.** On Hermes 0.21.3 the host rewrites the process-global `TERMINAL_CWD` to the home directory during the first turn of a CLI session (`agent/relay_runtime.py` imports `gateway/run.py` lazily, and that module's import-time bridge applies the `Path.home()` fallback for an empty or placeholder `terminal.cwd`). `resolve_agent_cwd()` then named the home directory, the plugin hooks found no plan there and injected nothing, and nothing signalled that the plan in the launch directory had been skipped. Upstream: NousResearch/hermes-agent#86411 and #95577.

**What the fix does.** The rewrite runs before the first plugin hook, so the plugin cannot recover the root on its own and does not guess.

- When the resolved directory holds no plan and the launch directory of a CLI session does, `pre_llm_call` injects one line naming both directories and the `PWF_PLAN_ROOT` pin instead of returning nothing. The line is CLI-only and stays silent in `hermes -w` worktree sessions, for a launch directory without planning state, and for a launch directory whose session isolation refuses the session.
- `/pwf-status` prints the same line under `No planning files found.`, and `/pwf` appends it when the plan it created went somewhere other than a launch directory that already holds one.
- `/pwf` and `/pwf-status` honor `PWF_PLAN_ROOT` like the hooks. A pin that does not resolve is reported instead of creating or reading a plan in the directory Hermes named.
- `docs/hermes.md` documents the mechanism, what was reproduced with the 0.21.0 source, the pin for project-scoped CLI sessions, and the shell-hook route as the unaffected alternative.

Verified with the real `agent.runtime_cwd.resolve_agent_cwd()` from a Hermes 0.21.0 checkout driven with an empty `TERMINAL_CWD`: after the lazy import the resolver names the home directory, the first hook returns the notice, `post_tool_call` and `pre_verify` stay quiet, and with the pin the plan is injected. A healthy host (resolver agrees with the process cwd) sees no change in hook output.

### Thanks
- @ericshunhinglee-cloud, for the report with the setter stack trace, the on-the-wire token evidence and the upstream cross-references in #272.

name: v3.20.1 - four fixes from the v3.19.0 and v3.20.0 review issues
body:
Four fixes from the v3.19.0 release review, each with a regression test.

- `init-session.sh`: a plan name with an embedded newline created an unusable `.planning/<date>-line-one<newline>line-two/` directory and exited 1 with it left behind. The slug is now a single line, as in the PowerShell twin (#257).
- Both initializers bound `PLAN_ID` for the attestation call but not `PWF_PLAN_ROOT`, so a pin inherited from another project silently redirected or blocked the attestation of the plan that was just created. `init-session.sh` and `init-session.ps1` now bind `PWF_PLAN_ROOT` to the current project around the call and restore the inherited value afterwards (#261).
- `session-catchup.py`, OpenCode adapter: a part row whose `state` or `state.input` is not an object raised `AttributeError`, and a row whose `data` column is not valid JSON made SQLite raise `malformed JSON` for the whole session. Malformed shapes count as empty input, non-JSON rows are filtered with `json_valid(data)`, and healthy rows in the same session are still reported (#258).
- Hermes plugin: with two or more named plans under `.planning/` and no `PLAN_ID`, the plugin resolved the shared pointer or the newest plan by modification time, so two Hermes sessions on two plans in one project could receive each other's plan. It now applies the v3.17.1 rule: the one-line `Multiple plans are available` notice once per turn, nothing injected, and `/pwf-status`, `planning_with_files_status` and `planning_with_files_check_complete` report the missing selector. `PWF_PLAN_ROOT` pins the project root and does not choose one of several same-root plans (#264).

Thanks
- @ShaunLinTW for the OpenCode catchup guards and tests in #263.

name: v3.20.0 - DeepSeek Harness first-class support and Cursor named plans on Windows
body:
## DeepSeek Harness becomes a first-class host

DSH reads the skill from `~/.agents/skills/` but ignores the `hooks:` block in SKILL.md, so the plan was never injected there. v3.20.0 adds a native Cordis plugin, `dsh-planning-with-files` (source in `.dsh/packages/dsh-planning-with-files/`), that carries the lifecycle: the framed plan on every prompt (`agent/pre-step`), the compaction note plus a fresh plan after a completed compaction (`session/event`, `compaction/end`), the progress reminder after `write` and `edit` (`tools/post-execute`), and the completion gate at the turn boundary in gated mode (`agent/turn-stopping`) with the shared `.stop_blocks` cap and stall detection. `/pwf` and `/pwf-status` are DSH commands, `pwf_init`, `pwf_status` and `pwf_check` are tools, and DSH's own `/plan` is untouched. Install:

```
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-planning-with-files
```

then restart `dsh web`; the same command serves the `headless`, `sdk` and `acp` profiles. Verified against the published `@deepseek-ai/dsh` 0.1.5-rc.2 with real model calls: the plan block reaches the model request, the gate steers once and stops at the cap, nothing is injected without a plan or with `PLANNING_DISABLED=1`. Guide: `docs/deepseek-harness.md`. Closes #252.

## Cursor named plans on Windows

Cursor's native PowerShell hooks now resolve named plans through the shared `resolve-plan-dir.ps1`: `PLAN_ID` is binding, `PWF_PLAN_ROOT` pins the project, one named plan resolves through `.active_plan` or on its own, two or more require `PLAN_ID`, a stale pointer falls through to the root plan like `inject-plan.sh`. The bash hooks keep reading the root `task_plan.md` only. PR #251 by @kuei51307-hub, item 9 of #250; the other items of #250 are now separate issues #253 to #261.

## Fixes

- `resolve-plan-dir.ps1` and `attest-plan.ps1` no longer call `[IO.Path]::IsPathFullyQualified`, which does not exist on Windows PowerShell 5.1, so a `PWF_PLAN_ROOT` pin works on 5.1 again.
- The PowerShell resolver tests paths literally; a project path containing `[` or `]` resolves its plans under pwsh.
- A zero-byte `.active_plan` no longer raises in `resolve-plan-dir.ps1`, `ledger-append.ps1`, `ledger-summary.ps1` and `phase-status.ps1`.
- The OpenCode plugin (1.1.0) and the DSH plugin apply the v3.17.1 rule: several named plans without `PLAN_ID` get the `Multiple plans are available` notice instead of a guessed plan.
- Cursor PowerShell hooks survive ConstrainedLanguage mode, send UTF-8, always print the `preToolUse` decision, and name the offending `PWF_PLAN_ROOT` or `PLAN_ID` value in their notices.

## README

One "The 3-file pattern" block replaces five introductory sections, a "First-class hosts" table replaces the Hermes section, and the per-host command tables sit in one collapsible. Old anchors keep working.

## Thanks

- @kuei51307-hub for the Cursor PowerShell named-plan resolution and the 5.1 fix in #251.
- @loarland for reporting the DeepSeek Harness gap in #252.

name: v3.19.0 - PowerShell named plans, exact catchup filenames, safe active-pointer replacement
body:
## What changed

### PowerShell named plans
`init-session.ps1` now has the same named-plan flow as the shell initializer. A positional project name or `-PlanDir` creates an isolated `.planning\<date>-<slug>\` plan with collision suffixes, records the shared `.active_plan` pointer, inherits the root `.mode` policy floor, and keeps `-Template`, `-Autonomous` and `-Gated` working. Zero-argument root mode is unchanged. Attestation runs through `attest-plan.ps1` on Windows and `attest-plan.sh` elsewhere, bound to the plan that was just created (#247). Plan ids stay ASCII for names with letters that .NET folds to ASCII, plan files are written with literal paths so a project path containing `[` or `]` works under pwsh, and an empty name stays in root mode.

Behaviour change: a positional name passed to `init-session.ps1` now creates a named plan instead of writing the project root. The Cursor native PowerShell hooks still read only the root `task_plan.md`, so Cursor users on Windows who want hook injection should keep using zero-argument root mode for now.

### Session catchup anchors only on exact planning filenames
A write to a lookalike such as `draft_task_plan.md` or `archive-progress.md` no longer counts as a planning update that moves the recovery window forward and hides later context. The OpenCode SQLite lookup is bounded to exact planning paths, revalidated after decoding, iterated lazily, and now case-sensitive like the JSONL scanners. The rule covers the canonical copies, the Hermes, MastraCode and OpenCode adapters (#248), the root `scripts/session-catchup.py` used by the Claude Code plugin, and the five translated copies; a new test loads every shipped copy so the boundary cannot drift again.

### Safe active-pointer replacement in both initializers
`init-session.sh` no longer writes `.planning/.active_plan` with shell redirection in slug mode. It verifies the physical planning root and the existing pointer through the selector before creating anything and replaces the pointer through the selector's contained atomic update: a hardlinked pointer keeps its peer intact, a symlinked or non-regular pointer is refused before a plan directory exists, and a planning root that resolves outside the project stops initialization (#249). `init-session.ps1` applies the same rule through `set-active-plan.ps1`.

New selector mode: `set-active-plan.sh --verify-root` and `set-active-plan.ps1 -VerifyRoot` check the planning root and the shared pointer in constant time without listing or selecting. The replaced pointer keeps a umask-derived mode instead of the 0600 that `mktemp` creates, and an unreadable pointer no longer aborts plan listing.

## Verification
All five CI jobs (Linux, Windows and macOS pytest, Pi extension, OpenCode plugin) passed on the release candidate and on the final master commit. Each PR was reproduced against v3.18.3 before merging, and three independent reviews plus an adversarial verification of the maintainer follow-ups ran before the tag.

## Thanks
- @ShaunLinTW for the PowerShell slug-mode initializer, host-aware attestation and the Windows PowerShell regression suite (#247).
- @kuei51307-hub for the exact planning filename boundary across the catchup scanners (#248) and the safe active-pointer replacement (#249).

name: v3.18.3 - Quiet completion notices

Completed plans no longer emit the routine completion notice through the shared Stop gate or Codex Stop hook. Claude Code plugin and standalone skill hooks inherit the quieter successful-completion behavior.

Explicit check-complete commands without the gate flag still report completion. Incomplete-plan notices, gate block decisions, recursion protection, block caps, stall diagnostics and plan selection safeguards are unchanged.

The shell and PowerShell changes are synchronized across maintained canonical mirrors. Regression coverage exercises repeated successful checks, preserves existing gate state, and verifies that incomplete gated plans still request continuation.

name: v3.18.1 - UTF-8 BOM active-pointer compatibility
body:
Fix active-plan display and listing when `.planning/.active_plan` starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark, as written by some Windows editors and PowerShell UTF-8 workflows. The shell helper now recognizes the valid plan name while preserving the pointer file and existing slug and project-containment checks.

name: v3.18.0: Saved plan inventory
body:
Saved named plans can now be listed with `sh scripts/set-active-plan.sh --list` or PowerShell `scripts/set-active-plan.ps1 -List`. The output shows each plan ID, phase counts, and the shared default pointer, making it easier to choose a `PLAN_ID` before starting a session.

Counts handle mixed status formats, duplicate markers, and the templates shipped in all six languages. Code examples and unrelated sections do not count as phases. Directory, plan-file, and pointer reads are checked against the current project's filesystem boundary. Pointer updates use atomic replacement to preserve hardlinked files and report write failures accurately.

The helpers and usage instructions ship across the canonical skill, plugin scripts, and supported IDE bundles, including OpenCode, Mastracode, and Hermes. Kiro's separate `.kiro/plan` layout is documented separately. Listing is read-only and does not select a plan or attach a session.

name: v3.17.1 - Fail closed on ambiguous named plans
body:
Multiple named plans in one project now require `PLAN_ID`, even when `.planning/sessions/` does not exist. This fixes #240: a shared `.active_plan` pointer or newest-plan fallback could redirect a Codex session after compaction.

UserPromptSubmit explains the missing pin. Per-tool and PreCompact hooks remain quiet, while Stop and attestation refuse to use an unrelated root plan. The shell, PowerShell and Python paths agree. Explicit pins, single named plans and legacy root plans remain supported.

Set `PLAN_ID` in the environment that launches each host. Setting it inside a tool subprocess does not update an already-running host.

### Validation
All five [GitHub CI jobs](https://github.com/OthmanAdi/planning-with-files/actions/runs/34214951641) passed on e8ad1534ed4f321cad83f900d2775144b860d6f1: Ubuntu 758 tests, macOS 760 tests, Windows 773 tests, plus the Pi and OpenCode suites.

The v3.17.1 tag was updated from 5046267 to e8ad153 to include the corrected BSD-userland test expectation. The test verifies refusal with two named plans and BSD stat discovery with one live plan. Packaged runtime files are unchanged.

### Thanks
@sunznx for the regression report and deterministic reproduction in #240.

name: v3.17.0 - Claude Code hooks in one Python process
body:
Every Claude Code hook fire forked about 130 processes. On Linux and macOS a fork costs a few milliseconds and nobody noticed. Under Git Bash on Windows a fork costs about 90 ms, so a prompt paid 7 to 12 seconds against the 10 second hook timeout, Claude Code printed "UserPromptSubmit hook timed out after 10s - output discarded", the plan never reached the model, and every Bash, Read, Grep and Edit call waited 5 more seconds in PreToolUse. Found on the maintainer's own machine the day after 3.16.1 shipped.

### Fixed
- The events now run in one Python process. `scripts/inject-plan.py` is a byte-identical twin of `inject-plan.sh` plus the dispatcher logic of `hooks/claude-hook.sh`. The launcher finds a CPython 3 on PATH with a fork-free walk (absolute entries only, Microsoft Store aliases skipped, `python3` preferred over `python`), runs the twin with `python -I -B`, and falls back to the unchanged shell chain on any non-zero exit. `PWF_FAST_PATH=0` forces the shell chain. Measured on the reporting machine: UserPromptSubmit 8.1 s, 10.2 s and 7.1 s before, 0.33 s after; PreToolUse 5.5 s before, about 0.3 s after.
- The standalone skill route uses the same twin once a plan is accepted, with a fork-free interpreter discovery. A directory without planning state answers before any fork on both routes.
- Both routes share one turn-marker slot and one progress-guard slot per plan: the launcher hands the twin the shell's own `$PWD` spelling.
- Characters outside the Basic Multilingual Plane survive the plugin's JSON encoder on Windows; the `awk` walk now runs byte-wise.

### Security
- Hook interpreters start in isolated mode. The `python -` heredocs and `-c` snippets in `inject-plan.sh`, `resolve-plan-dir.sh` and `skill-hook.sh` put the current directory first on `sys.path`, so a repository carrying its own `secrets.py`, `hashlib.py` or `ctypes.py` had that file imported by the hook on every prompt. Every interpreter start in those scripts and in the twin now passes `-I`, and a test plants six such modules and proves neither route runs them.

### Verification
- `tests/test_inject_plan_python_parity.py` runs the shell reference and the twin over the same fixtures and asserts identical stdout for every context and event, including the five divergences a second-model review found before release (NUL bytes in `.active_plan`, the awk `phases: /N` quirk, the CRLF progress tail under Git for Windows' sed, cache-slot spelling, non-BMP characters). Launcher tests prove the fast path runs, falls back, and never selects a Store alias or a relative PATH entry.
- Not changed in this release: the Stop hook still runs the shell chain, and the Codex, Gemini and GitHub Copilot shell adapters still start their interpreters in default mode.

name: v3.16.1 - Session isolation and hook delivery
body:
What changed:

- Claude plugin and standalone hook JSON preserve literal backslashes under POSIX awk, including Windows paths.
- Attached Codex, Hermes and Pi sessions now require PLAN_ID when their project contains multiple plans. An attachment authorizes a session; it does not choose a plan. Shared standalone hooks apply the same guard.
- Standalone skill hooks read the host's JSON session identity, send PreToolUse and PostToolUse instructions through additionalContext, and throttle the progress reminder per turn. Opt-out, rejected selectors and unsafe cache paths are covered by regression tests.
- The native Codex progress reminder now uses the same session ID for writing and resetting its cache entry.
- Installed packages include the advertised loop template and the complete hook dependency chain. Recovery instructions follow the selected task directory and preserve existing planning files.
- Documentation states the limits of local hash attestation, PreCompact output and the advisory write guard. Shared planning files require one writer; worker ledgers or files keep concurrent reports separate.

Thanks: @hzura and @wangxiaodong1021 for the parallel-session reports in #50, @sortakool for #239, and @oaabahussain for the trust-boundary discussion in #150.

Verification: all five [CI jobs at the released commit](https://github.com/OthmanAdi/planning-with-files/actions/runs/33990436415) passed, covering the full Python suite on Linux, macOS and Windows, plus 54 Pi tests and 34 OpenCode tests. ClawHub staging verifies all 31 canonical files.

name: v3.16.0: the PostToolUse nudge reaches the model, once per turn
body:
The PostToolUse progress reminder was addressed to Claude and delivered to the user instead, on every matching tool call, with `Bash` in the matcher. Reported by @sortakool in #239, filed shortly after #236 to #238 and fixed on its own.

### Fixed
- **The PostToolUse nudge never reached the model (closes #239, reported by @sortakool).** `hooks/claude-hook.sh:110` emitted "Update progress.md with what you just did" as `systemMessage`, which Claude Code documents as a warning shown to the user. So the person saw the instruction after every `Write`, `Edit` and `Bash` call and the model, which the sentence is written for, never saw it once. `emit_session_start` eleven lines above already emitted `hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` for its own event, so the correct shape was in the same file the whole time. Both the plugin dispatcher and `.codex/hooks/post_tool_use.py` now emit `additionalContext` with `"hookEventName": "PostToolUse"`; the Codex adapter's `pre_tool_use.py` and `run_sh.py` already used that shape for their events.
- **The nudge is now once per turn rather than once per tool call.** The string is a constant, so every repeat after the first carries no information: it names no tool, no file and no phase. UserPromptSubmit and SessionStart fire once per turn and clear a marker; the first post-tool fire of the turn sets it. The marker lives in the user's private cache under `pwf-turn/`, never in the plan directory, and is keyed on the plan path plus `PWF_SESSION_ID` so two sessions sharing a plan do not silence each other. A cache root that cannot be created skips the throttle rather than the reminder, so a broken cache cannot quietly remove it.
- **`Bash` came off the PostToolUse matchers.** `ls`, `git status` and `grep` were tripping a "you changed something, record it" reminder. `hooks/hooks.json` goes to `Write|Edit` and both Codex manifests go to `apply_patch|Edit|Write`. PreToolUse keeps `Bash`: a plan reminder before a shell command is a different and wanted behavior. The standalone skill route already used `Write|Edit`, which is further evidence the wider matcher was drift rather than intent.
- **The plugin dispatcher still had the #237 fallback.** `active_plan_dir()` in `hooks/claude-hook.sh` resolves through the shared resolver and then fell back to the legacy root `task_plan.md`, the fallback v3.15.0 removed from the script and Codex routes but not from this one. Found while fixing #239. A rejected `PLAN_ID` or `PWF_PLAN_ROOT` now stops there too.

### Verification
- 10 new tests in `tests/test_post_tool_nudge.py`, driving both routes as processes. Coverage includes the field, the once-per-turn behavior through a real re-arm, session-start as a second re-arm, two session ids not silencing each other, a broken cache root still emitting, and every matcher in all three manifests.
- One test earns its place by proving key agreement through deletion: the two Codex scripts derive the marker key independently and one of them resolves a `PWF_PLAN_ROOT` pin while the other does not. A divergence there would leave the marker uncleared and silently degrade the nudge to once per session, so the re-arm is asserted to remove the exact file the throttle wrote.

### Not changed
- The standalone skill route emits the same sentence as plain stdout from a YAML frontmatter scalar, with no throttle. It already carries the narrower `Write|Edit` matcher, so the spam this issue is about never applied to it, and giving it the throttle means either embedding cache-key logic in a hook scalar or routing it through a new script context across eleven SKILL.md files. Both are real changes that belong in a release where they can be tested on their own rather than appended to a fix.
- `FileChanged` was suggested in the issue as a way to catch a `Bash` command that rewrites a file. It is a new event surface with its own behavior and is deliberately left for its own release.

### Thanks
- Raymond, for tracing all three defects to the line and checking the Codex route before filing, and for confirming there was no user-side workaround rather than leaving it to be guessed at (#239).

name: v3.15.0: explicit plan selectors bind, root .mode is a floor
body:
Three selector and policy defects reported by @sortakool, all reproduced here before any code changed. Two of them let a session work on a plan nobody selected, and the third made the diagnostic that should have caught them report PASS. A minor rather than a patch because two behaviors change on purpose: a `PLAN_ID` that does not resolve now refuses instead of picking another plan, and a slug plan can no longer start below a project's committed `.mode`.

### Security
- **A `PLAN_ID` that named no directory attested and injected a different plan at rc=0 (closes #237, reported by @sortakool).** `commands/plan-attest.md` has promised since v3.9.0 that an explicit selector which does not resolve exits with an error and never falls back to another plan. The `PWF_PLAN_ROOT` half held. The `PLAN_ID` half did not: `resolve_from_env` returned 1 both when no selector was set and when the selector was rejected, so a one-character typo fell through to `.active_plan`, then to newest-by-mtime, and `attest-plan.sh` locked that other plan without a word. The guard in `attest-plan.sh` written for exactly this case was unreachable, because the resolver never returned empty. A non-empty `PLAN_ID` is now a binding in every resolver: it resolves or it stops, whether it was rejected for slug shape, for naming no directory, or for failing containment. An empty value still means unset. Fixed in `resolve-plan-dir.sh`, `resolve-plan-dir.ps1`, the inline resolver inside `inject-plan.sh`, the three PowerShell helpers that carry their own, and the Hermes, OpenCode and Pi plugin resolvers.
- **A slug plan with no `.mode` bypassed the project's root `.mode` (closes #238, reported by @sortakool).** A project makes attestation mandatory by committing a root `.mode`, which is a reviewed project setting. `inject-plan.sh` read the slug's `.mode` and never the root's, and `init-session.sh` writes no `.mode` unless `--autonomous` or `--gated` was passed, so `init-session.sh <name>`, which `/plan` runs, produced a plan with no attestation requirement and full injection. The project's policy was a flag the agent chose at plan creation. The root `.mode` is now a floor: strictness-raising tokens count from either file, so a slug may raise but never lower, and the one strictness-lowering token, `plan-guard-off`, needs the root's agreement. The same floor applies to the completion gate in `check-complete.sh` and `check-complete.ps1`, which read `.mode` the same way and had the same bypass. `init-session.sh` also seeds a new slug from the root `.mode` so the effective policy is visible in the plan directory, not only in the resolver.
- **Every consumer that reads or writes the selected plan now refuses a rejected selector instead of falling back to the cwd.** `check-complete.sh` would have reported the root plan's completion state, which decides whether an autonomous run may stop; `ledger-summary.sh` would have fed the loop another plan's phase counts; `phase-status.sh` and `ledger-append.sh` would have written into a plan the operator never named. Each says which selector refused rather than going quietly dark.
- **The five Codex hooks had the same fallback.** They call the shared resolver directly rather than `inject-plan.sh`, so they inherited the refusal but then fell through to the legacy root `task_plan.md`: `stop.sh` would have decided whether the run may stop from the wrong plan, and `pre-compact.sh` would have carried the wrong plan through the one moment a session cannot re-read it. All five now stop, and `user-prompt-submit.sh`, which fires once per turn, prints the same notice as `inject-plan.sh` so the session is never dark without a stated cause.

### Fixed
- **`plan-doctor.sh` reported PASS on a fully dark-hooks state (closes #236, reported by @sortakool).** The injection check substring-matched five control strings against output that carries the plan body verbatim inside the `===BEGIN-PWF-DATA===` fences, which produced two defects. A plan whose phase line read "fix the false PLAN TAMPERED warning in plan-doctor" reported a hash mismatch while correctly attested, and no documentation reserved those phrases. Worse, the `PWF_PLAN_ROOT` arm matched `PWF_PLAN_ROOT is not a directory`, which is not a substring of the text `inject-plan.sh` emits, so the arm was dead code and execution fell through to the success arm: `PWF_PLAN_ROOT=/nonexistent` printed `PASS injection: emits plan context (123 bytes)` while nothing was injected at all, counting the refusal notice's own bytes as plan context. The file's own comment four lines above already warned that reporting a refusal's byte count as PASS tells a dark user their hooks are fine. Classification now branches on the frame: every refusal path exits before `frame_file` runs, so a frame proves injection happened, and unframed output is by construction a notice. The default arm warns, so a future reworded or translated banner degrades noisily instead of silently. The stale literal is corrected against the emitting `echo`.
- **`attest-plan.sh` reported "No task_plan.md found" when a selector was refused.** True but misleading: the plan exists and the selector was the problem. It now names the selector that refused.

### Changed
- v3.14.0 made the Hermes and OpenCode resolvers fall through on an unresolvable `PLAN_ID`, to match `resolve-plan-dir.sh`. That parity was correct and the target was wrong. All three plugin resolvers now bind instead, along with the shell.
- The Hermes and OpenCode plugins apply the root `.mode` floor as well, so `mode_tokens` and `modeTokens` take the project root alongside the plan directory. A malformed root `.mode` on the OpenCode side returns the same "not allowed" signal a malformed slug `.mode` already produced, which fails the plan closed rather than treating an unreadable policy as no policy.
- Version bumped to 3.15.0 across the tracked parity set and the ClawHub stage. The OpenCode plugin package goes to 1.0.1 and the Pi extension to 1.2.5, since both changed.

### Verification
- Python suite 653 to 696 tests, plus 28 to 34 in the OpenCode Vitest suite. New files `test_plan_selector_binding.py`, `test_root_mode_floor.py` and `test_plan_doctor_classification.py`; new arms in `test_resolver_parity.py`, `test_resolve_plan_dir.py`, `test_resolver_plan_root_pin.py`, `test_hermes_first_class.py` and the OpenCode suite. Five existing tests asserted the fall-through and were rewritten to assert the refusal, keeping their original security assertion intact.
- Each suite carries its own control arm, because two of the first drafts passed on fixtures that could not have failed: a completion-gate assertion over a plan with every phase complete, where the gate resolves to advisory whether or not it is armed, and a parallel-write-guard assertion over a plan with nothing checked to lose.
- The `plan-doctor` suite drives the real `inject-plan.sh` rather than a synthetic string, since literal drift is the actual defect, and adds a stub that emits an unknown banner to pin the drift property itself.
- All three issues were reproduced on Windows with Git Bash before the fix and re-run after, including @sortakool's control arms.

### Thanks
- Raymond, for three issues filed separately so each could be fixed and verified on its own, each with a control arm, a traced mechanism, and in #236 both a suggested patch and the more robust alternative that was taken instead (#236, #237, #238).

name: v3.14.0: first-class OpenCode support through its own plugin system
body:
OpenCode becomes a first-class host through its own plugin system, and issue #235 is fixed. Verified against OpenCode 1.18.21: the plugin loaded from a project config directory, `pwf_init`, `pwf_status` and `pwf_check` appeared in the tool list, `/pwf` and `/pwf-status` in the command list, and a real session message received the framed plan as a synthetic part.

## Install on OpenCode

```bash
npx skills add OthmanAdi/planning-with-files --skill planning-with-files -g
```

Then add the plugin to `opencode.json` (project) or `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` (global):

```json
{ "plugin": ["opencode-planning-with-files"] }
```

Full guide: docs/opencode.md.

## Added

- **Native OpenCode plugin `opencode-planning-with-files`** (`.opencode/packages/opencode-planning-with-files/`, TypeScript, npm). `chat.message` appends the framed active plan to every user message (or a once-per-turn ambiguity notice); `tool.execute.after` appends the progress reminder to write, edit, patch, multiedit and apply_patch output; `experimental.session.compacting` keeps the plan pointer and attestation hash in the compaction context; `event` on `session.idle` runs the completion gate in gated mode and re-prompts the session with the gate reason (Tier 2, follow-up inject). Tools `pwf_init` (root or `.planning/<date>-<slug>/`, `mode: autonomous` or `gated` with the v3 markers and attestation), `pwf_status`, `pwf_check`. Each session resolves its plan from its own directory; child sessions are never re-prompted.
- **Parity with the shell route in TypeScript**: `resolve-plan-dir.sh` precedence with slug validation, link refusal and containment, BOM-tolerant `.active_plan`; the `inject-plan.sh` nested-root rule; the `check-complete.sh --gate` decision table with the shared `.stop_blocks` and `.gate_last_ledger` files; the `init-session.sh` markers; the same frame format and attestation refusal.
- **Commands** `.opencode/commands/pwf.md` and `pwf-status.md`, a dogfood entry that loads the plugin from source when this repository is opened in OpenCode, 27 Vitest tests and a `vitest (OpenCode plugin)` CI job.

## Fixed

- `docs/opencode.md` named the wrong install location (closes #235, reported by @luyanfeng): `npx skills add -g` installs to `~/.agents/skills/`, which OpenCode reads natively. The page, the OpenCode skill's restore-context snippets and its file-location table now name the real paths.
- OpenCode was listed as an Enhanced host on the strength of `hooks:` frontmatter OpenCode never runs. The tier tables, MIGRATION.md and the README now say what each install actually gets.
- Hermes: a `PLAN_ID` that did not resolve blacked out injection; both the Hermes and the OpenCode resolver now fall through like `resolve-plan-dir.sh`.

## Verification

name: v3.13.0: first-class Hermes Agent support (CLI and Desktop)
body:
Hermes Agent by Nous Research becomes a first-class host, on the CLI and in Hermes Desktop. Everything below was checked against the Hermes v0.19.1 source and a live install: the plugin was loaded through Hermes' own plugin manager, and the skill bundle was scanned with Hermes' skills-guard.

## Install on Hermes

```bash
hermes skills install OthmanAdi/planning-with-files/.hermes/skills/planning-with-files --yes
hermes plugins install OthmanAdi/planning-with-files/.hermes/plugins/planning-with-files
hermes plugins enable planning-with-files
```

Full guide: docs/hermes.md.

## Added

- **Hermes plugin 0.2.0.** Resolves `.planning/<slug>/` plans (`PLAN_ID`, `.planning/.active_plan`, newest slug, legacy root) with the same slug validation, containment and ambiguity rule as the shell resolver. Before this release the adapter only saw a root `task_plan.md`. Honors `PWF_PLAN_ROOT` (fail-closed) and `PLANNING_DISABLED=1`.
- **Completion gate on Hermes** through the `pre_verify` hook: while an `in_progress` phase remains in a gated plan, the plugin asks Hermes to keep going. Same decision table and state files as `check-complete.sh --gate`, implemented in Python so Hermes Desktop on Windows needs no `sh`. Bounded by Hermes' `agent.max_verify_nudges` (default 3 per turn) and fired only on turns that changed files, so Hermes is Tier 2 (follow-up inject).
- **`/pwf`, `/pwf-status`, `/plan-status`** as real in-session commands (CLI, gateway, Desktop). `/pwf --gated Night run` creates an isolated plan, writes the v3 markers and attests it. `planning_with_files_init` gained `name` and `mode`. Hermes' own `/plan` skill is not shadowed.
- **Bundled skill registration** (`planning-with-files:planning-with-files`), a Python completion check when `sh` is absent, and a shell-hook bridge (`shell_hook.py`) for config-file hooks driving the canonical scripts.
- **tests/test_hermes_first_class.py**, 18 tests covering the resolver, the gate, init markers, registration, commands, the fallback and the bridge.
- README: new sections on long-running reliability, Hermes support, and multi-agent runs.

## Fixed

- The `.hermes` SKILL.md pointed Windows users at `~\.hermes`; native Windows Hermes lives under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\hermes`.
- `.hermes/commands/*.md` were never loaded by Hermes (no Markdown command loader exists); the plugin registers the commands now.
- docs/hermes.md claimed Hermes had no stop-hook equivalent; it documents `pre_verify`, Desktop, Windows, the shell-hook route and `hermes import-agent claude-code`. The canonical `skills/planning-with-files` path is refused by Hermes' skills-guard scanner; the `.hermes` bundle is the supported path and scans SAFE.

## Changed

- README reorganized: install routes and the collapsible platform and FAQ sections first, benchmarks, repository layout, releases and community at the bottom. Nothing removed.
- Hermes Agent listed under Tier 2 in the host capability tables (English SKILL.md copies and MIGRATION.md).
- Version 3.13.0 across the tracked parity set and the ClawHub stage.

## Verification

- 60 existing Hermes-related tests plus 18 new ones pass; the full suite is green.
- Live load in the Hermes 0.19.1 plugin manager: three hooks, three commands and the bundled skill registered; gated init, injection with plan id, gate continuation, tamper refusal and reminder delivery observed.
- `hermes skills install` of the `.hermes` bundle succeeds from the hub with a SAFE verdict.

name: v3.11.1: the Copilot error hook parses under a POSIX shell
body:
### Fixed

**The GitHub Copilot error hook could not be parsed by a POSIX shell (PR #228 by @dylanpulver).**

`error-occurred.sh` fed both of its Python helpers with `<<<`, a bash here-string that dash does not implement. The test suite invokes the shell hooks as `sh script`, so the `#!/bin/bash` shebang never applied, and on ubuntu runners, where `/bin/sh` is dash, the file died at line 32 with `Syntax error: redirection unexpected`. Master CI had failed on that leg for five consecutive runs. Both call sites now pipe with `printf '%s\n'`.

The four sibling hooks pipe with `echo`, and that form was deliberately not copied. Under dash, builtin `echo` expands backslash escapes, so an escaped newline inside an error message comes back as a real control character and `json.load` rejects it. Copying it would have traded a loud syntax error for a silent parse failure.

No user was affected, because `.github/hooks/planning-with-files.json` invokes the hook under a `bash` key that bypasses both the shebang and the exec bit. This is a CI and portability fix.

Also repairs the v3.11.0 changelog entry, which warned against emitting JSON with `echo` and then carried two raw newlines of its own, inside the code spans for the escape sequence it was describing.

### Verification

Checked against real dash rather than taken from the report. Pre-fix the hook exits 2 with the CI error verbatim, post-fix it exits 0 and emits valid JSON with the newline escaped as two characters. All five scripts in `.github/hooks/scripts/` now parse under a POSIX shell, where before this was the only one that failed. Full Python suite: 434 passed, 10 skipped, 497 subtests passed.

### Thanks

@dylanpulver found this in CI rather than in a bug report, reproduced the ubuntu condition locally instead of working from the log, confirmed the suite genuinely exercises the path by reverting his own change, and declined the fix that would have looked right.

name: v3.11.0: one skill instead of six
body:
The Claude Code plugin now registers one skill instead of six. Nothing was deleted, nothing was renamed, and every install command is unchanged.

### What changed

The five language variants moved from `skills/planning-with-files-<lang>/` to `skills/i18n/planning-with-files-<lang>/`. One directory of depth is the whole mechanism: Claude Code discovers a plugin's skills by scanning `skills/*/SKILL.md` at a single level and does not recurse, while `npx skills add` resolves `--skill` by skill name across a recursive scan and does not care about depth.

`/plan-ar`, `/plan-de`, `/plan-es`, `/plan-zh` and `/plan-zht` now read their translated skill from disk, and each one states that the status tokens stay literal English because `check-complete.sh` matches them with `grep -F`.

### Measured, not inferred

Against the real Claude Code loader:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| Registered plugin skills | 6 | **1** |
| Components | 19 | 14 |
| Always-on tokens per session | ~2,254 | **~1,042** |

All thirteen slash commands survive. The skills CLI still discovers all seven skills by name, and `npx skills add OthmanAdi/planning-with-files --skill planning-with-files-de` installs to the same destination as before with the full 20-script surface and pulls in nothing else.

### Also in this release

- **`docs/languages.md`**, the page the translations never had. `docs/` carried a setup guide for every supported IDE and nothing for languages.
- **Seven shell hooks could emit JSON with a raw control character on macOS.** They interpolated a `json.dumps` result and emitted it with `echo`; under `sh` on macOS, where `/bin/sh` is bash in POSIX mode with `xpg_echo`, `echo` turns the escaped newline back into a real one. All seven now use `printf '%s\n'`.

Full suite 434 passed, 10 skipped, 497 subtests.

### Known limitation

An existing variant install records the old path in its skills lock file, so `npx skills update` cannot resolve it until the skill is reinstalled. The installed skill keeps working and a fresh install always works. Nothing in this change could avoid that; it is inherent to moving a directory.

### Thanks

This took four attempts across seven months of the issue tracker, so credit goes to everyone who pushed on it.

- @sean3808 opened #130 in April with the analysis that framed the whole problem: identical scripts and templates, prose the only real difference, and five skill descriptions loaded into every session that most users would never invoke. Every later attempt is a variation on that report.
- @dylanpulver wrote the answer that shipped (#226). He found the one-level plugin scan, checked the install route instead of assuming it, and carried the literal English status-token warning into all five commands where an earlier attempt had not. He also named the one cost he could not remove, which is what made the change reviewable, and diagnosed the macOS `echo` bug while rebasing.
- @SomSamantray audited the five variants against the canonical skill in #216 and proved the drift #130 predicted: twelve missing scripts, a missing Windows UTF-8 fix, and sync tooling covering only three dispatch targets. That shipped as v3.10.0 and had to land before this change was safe.
- @oaabahussain asked in #151 for a single canonical source with a CI parity gate. The gate shipped in v2.37.0 and is why this move could be verified rather than hoped at.
- @back1ply (#53) and @tiptinker (#47) filed the earliest two reports about the same duplication from the other direction, and are why `scripts/sync-ide-folders.py` exists.

### Why this took so long

The obvious fix was to delete the five directories, and it was proposed more than once. It could not be taken. Skill listings on a public directory cannot be retracted once published, so deleting the folders would not have removed the entries. It would have left five permanent listings whose install command had started to fail, which is worse for the people using them than either keeping or removing them. The variants also have real users who chose them deliberately, and breaking a working install is not a reasonable price for a packaging problem.

What was needed was a route that changes nothing anyone depends on, and it took until #226 to find one. The delay was not doubt about whether the problem was real. It was refusing to fix it by breaking installs.

name: v3.10.2: the opt-out reaches Copilot and Cursor
body:
`PLANNING_DISABLED=1` had never reached the GitHub Copilot or Cursor hooks. Both routes read `task_plan.md` directly instead of dispatching to `scripts/inject-plan.sh`, which is where the #195 guard lives, so eighteen hook entry points ignored the opt-out: a one-shot task sharing a working directory with an unrelated plan had no way to detach from it.

### Fixed

- **Copilot: all ten hook entry points now honour the opt-out** (PR #223, by @Whxuan0701).
- **Cursor: all eight hooks now honour it too.** Each guard reproduces its own hook's no-plan-file output, so the protocol shape is unchanged. `PreToolUse` still answers `{"decision": "allow"}` because that is what it emits unconditionally today, and the other three stay silent. `.gemini` is deliberately behind and is not covered.
- **Disabling the skill was making Copilot's `PreToolUse` more permissive, not neutral.** The merged guard answered `permissionDecision: allow` on the disabled path, so a user who set the variable to turn planning off also handed every tool call a blanket approval. Both copies now emit `{}`.
- **The Copilot PowerShell stop hook reported "Task incomplete (0/0 phases done)" on a plan with no phase headings** (PR #222, by @Whxuan0701). The #191 guard had reached `agent-stop.sh` and never its PowerShell twin.
- **`.cursor/hooks/stop.ps1` was the last copy the #191 fix never reached.** A repository-wide sweep of every script that emits a `(N/M phases done)` message now finds no unguarded copy left.
- **The Copilot PowerShell error hook had never logged an error on Windows.** `error-occurred.ps1` read stdin into `$input`, PowerShell's automatic pipeline variable, and under `-File` the assignment does not stick, so the JSON parse always saw an empty string.
- **The Hermes determinism probe could not run without a `python` alias** (PR #224, by @Whxuan0701). It now reuses `sys.executable`.

### Changed

The opt-out tests run every hook twice, once with the variable unset and once with it set, and fail if the unset run is already inert. The merged versions asserted only the disabled run, which a fleet of hooks gutted to emit `{}` unconditionally also passed. That baseline is what caught the `$input` bug.

### Verification

430 passed, 11 skipped, 492 subtests passed, from a 424 / 11 / 474 baseline. Every fix was mutation-tested: stripping the ten Copilot guards fails 9 assertions, gutting the fleet fails 6, restoring `$input` fails the anti-vacuity baseline by name, and stripping the eight Cursor guards plus the `stop.ps1` phase guard fails 9. All four `.ps1` files carrying non-ASCII keep their UTF-8 BOM, every touched script is pure LF, `sh -n` parses all nine shell hooks, and `sync-ide-folders.py --verify` is clean.

### Thanks

@Whxuan0701 sent three single-commit PRs rather than one bundle, each with a test that executes the real script. Auditing them is what surfaced the Cursor route, the permission widening and the `$input` bug.
